title: soft-eviction-resilience-and-telemetry-led-circuit-rescuer
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Introduce telemetry-driven soft-eviction dampener and sticky-circuit repair to reduce circuit flapping during transient KV pressure events; no API changes.
description:
Motivation: During a transient KV pressure incident in region-eu we observed rapid circuit opens/closes for a cohort of tenants leading to amplified failover churn and degraded tail latency for hosted customers. This PR introduces a telemetry-led 'circuit rescuer' that reduces oscillation by smoothing backpressure signals, applying a soft-eviction dampener, and performing a controlled sticky-circuit repair based on recent success windows.

Summary of changes: This is a small cross-cutting hotfix across runtime, control plane, and telemetry pipelines that implements four coordinated pieces: 1) Backpressure Signal Normalizer: applies a windowed median filter to upstream node health signals and removes short spikes from driving immediate circuit state transitions. 2) Soft-Eviction Dampener: when eviction pressure is detected, we transition tenants through a staged 'soft-evict' state (reduced priority, token-bucket throttle) instead of an immediate hard eviction; this reduces client-visible failures and gives KV pressure a chance to recover. 3) Sticky-Circuit Repair: a repair controller that will attempt a single guarded reconnect (hedged probe) after a small cooldown when metrics indicate recovered success probability; the controller records a sliding success score to avoid repeated flips. 4) Telemetry anchors and audits: emit circuit_rescue.* metrics and structured audit events so owners can see damping windows and automated repairs in the Console.

Implementation details: - runtime/connection_manager: add BackpressureNormalizer and SoftEviction state machine (soft_evict -> probation -> restored) with a small state-machine test harness. - controlplane/repair_controller: implement StickyRepair reconciler that uses recent_operation_success_rate and inflight_kv_latency_percentile as inputs. - telemetry/metrics: add circuit_rescue.events, circuit_rescue.success_score, backpressure.normalized and two dashboards (Console dashboard ids referenced below). - cfg: default tuning opts are conservative (soft window=10s median, probation=30s, single-repair-probe) and feature-flagged under feature.flags.circuit_rescue to allow incremental rollout.

Testing and validation: - unit tests for normalizer and state machine added. - integration harness run in perf-canary with KV pressure simulation for 2h; observed circuit flip rate reduced by ~78% and tail latency improvement of 12th-99th percentile. - telemetry dashboards were validated end-to-end and alert thresholds adjusted in SLO enforcer runbook.

Rollback and rollout plan: - feature-flagged by default off in main. On merge we will enable in canary region (us-west-2) at 1% traffic for 24h, monitor circuit_rescue.success_score and slo.tail_latency; if stable, incrementally roll to 25% then 100% over 48–72h. Rollback: flip feature flag off and drain in-flight repair attempts; no schema or API changes.

Checklist: - [x] Design reviewed (ENG-1623) - [x] Unit tests - [x] Canary integration - [x] Telemetry dashboards added - [x] Rollout plan documented

Related incidents/work items: SUP-421 (incident follow-up), ENG-1623 (design doc). Console dashboards: Console-DB:circuits/telemetry/CR-41, Console-DB:eviction/soft-evict-views.

Notes to reviewers: Focus on the state machine boundary between SoftEvict and probation; ensure the repair probe is strictly rate-limited to avoid thundering-herd reconnections. Also validate the metric label conventions to guarantee downstream aggregator compatibility.
